title: Reading the Bible in story order
notes: Every chapter of the Bible is read once, in the order its story happened on this timeline: Scripture's own sequence first, then Ussher's Annals where Scripture does not fix it, as everywhere else on the site. Days are balanced by length (about 85 verses), and a chapter is never split. Genesis runs into Job, whom Ussher places at about 1635 BC, between Joseph and Moses. Psalm 90 comes with the death of Moses. David's psalms follow his life: those with a heading about Saul or Absalom sit beside those chapters, Psalms 105 and 96 with the ark and 1 Chronicles 16, the Asaph psalms beside Asaph's appointment, and the sons of Korah where Korah's descendants praise in 2 Chronicles 20. Psalm 22 is beside the cross, Psalm 16 beside Pentecost, and the Hallel (Psalms 113 to 118) beside the Last Supper. The Songs of Ascents and Psalm 107 come with the return from exile, Psalm 119 with Ezra reading the law, and Psalms 146 to 150 close the Old Testament story. Song of Solomon, Proverbs and Ecclesiastes sit with Solomon; Proverbs 25 to 31 come with Hezekiah, whose men copied them. Chronicles runs beside Samuel and Kings, and the first nine chapters of genealogy open David's story. Each prophet stands within the reigns his book names; Jeremiah and Ezekiel are interleaved, and Daniel is read in the order of its dates. Haggai, Zechariah, Ezra, Esther, Nehemiah and Malachi follow the Persian reigns. The four Gospels are woven into one account, whole chapters at a time. Acts carries Paul's letters where they were written, and James where the site dates it (about AD 49). Hebrews, the Peter and Jude letters, the letters of John and Revelation close the year. Some prophecy and poetry has no date, and those days carry no year.
